business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Games

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Free Trade Agreement between the Government of New Zealand and the Government of the People's Republic of China (2008)
Agreement between New Zealand and Australia on the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 95A-95W, as inserted by the Companies (Disclosure of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2017, establishing the government-only beneficial ownership register; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), ss 5, 10-42, 69-84, mandating customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence and record-keeping; Terrorism Suppression Act 2002 for UN sanctions implementation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of a New Zealand Limited Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for contracting states: original certificate issued by the Companies Office is certified and then apostilled by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) Authentications Unit. For non-party states only: after Companies Office issuance, authenticate through the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT), then present to the destination state's consulate in New Zealand for consular legalization. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: certified by the Companies Office and apostilled by DIA if the destination is an Apostille Convention member. Consular Legalization: certified by the Companies Office, authenticated by MFAT, then legalized by the destination state's embassy or consulate for non-member states. These two routes are parallel alternatives and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed directors and shareholders, executed before a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in New Zealand, then Hague Apostille by DIA if the destination is a member state; alternatively, notarization, MFAT authentication and destination consulate legalization for a non-member state. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Subscriber shareholders and first directors, as filed on the New Zealand Companies Register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by DIA for member states; or MFAT authentication followed by destination consular legalization for non-member states. The two procedures are alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the UBO's or company's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a bank in an Apostille member state, the bank document is notarized and apostilled by that state's competent authority. For a bank in a non-member state, the bank document is notarized locally and processed through consular legalization at the destination embassy. If the bank is in New Zealand, use DIA apostille for member states or MFAT/consulate legalization for non-member states. Never chain apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, directors, officers, authorized signatories and high-risk counterparties must be screened before incorporation and continuously thereafter against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade sanctions list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the HM Treasury consolidated list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Interpol notices; domestic PEP, international PEP, negative news, criminal and regulatory enforcement, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction indicators must be assessed. Enhanced due diligence is mandated for PEPs and for proceeds routed through Apple App Store, Google Play, or high-risk jurisdictions, with escalation to the AML compliance officer and records retained under the AML/CFT Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register, Companies Office of New Zealand (online Name Reservation and Company Registration portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use Latin (Roman) script; te reo Maori is permitted when rendered in Latin script; Chinese characters and other non-Latin scripts are not accepted for registration, so any foreign-language name must be transliterated into a Romanized English form and reserved in that form. The Companies Office applies a four-tier similarity test: exact name match; near-identical sound or spelling; likely confusion with an existing registered or reserved name; and prohibited or restricted token. The statutory suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' must be included and is disregarded in similarity comparisons.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation expires after 20 working days; it is not automatically renewable but may be re-sponsored by filing a new name reservation application with the same proposed name. Upon rejection, the applicant must within 15 working days submit a written appeal to the Companies Office Name Approval Committee, attaching a statutory declaration, evidence of distinct use, and any consents. The Committee must consider all four tiers; if rejected again, the applicant may apply to the Registrar for reconsideration and thereafter pursue judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox can satisfy the Companies Act 1993 registered office requirement if there is a dedicated physical street address in New Zealand, mail is received at that address, and service of legal process is accepted. However, the Inland Revenue Department will not accept a virtual mailbox alone as the principal place of business for GST or PAYE registration, and most New Zealand banks will reject a virtual-office-only structure for an MMORPG operating through Apple/Google payout rails because they require operational substance, local books and records, control over intellectual property, and a verifiable board/management presence. Virtual office use is therefore structurally permissible but operationally high-risk unless supplemented by a managed physical suite, local agent, and actual commercial decision-making in New Zealand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for physical inspection by New Zealand Inland Revenue Department and Companies Office: existence of premises signage, staff presence, computers and servers, physical books and records, local bank statements, board minutes, and GST/PAYE evidence. Quantified risk: approximately 10% per year for a compliant low-risk foreign-owned entity, rising to 30-50% if only a virtual mailbox is used, no local staffing exists, no accounting records are held in New Zealand, or tax refunds are repeatedly claimed. Municipal authorities rarely inspect, but IRD has entry and information-gathering powers under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Registrar of Companies may issue compliance notices under the Companies Act 1993.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance through New Zealand Companies Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee is levied by the Companies Office for online name reservation; legal or agent service fees, if any, are not part of the official tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of New Zealand Limited Company (Incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Companies (Fees) Regulations 2013: NZD 110.00 converted at approximately 0.62 USD/NZD, approximate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille / consular legalization of the mandatory 5-document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand notary public, Department of Internal Affairs and Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for five documents including notary attestations and state authentication fees; not a fixed statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, PEP and sanctions database screening of all shareholders and directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per entity/UBO screening through commercial screening databases such as World-Check or equivalent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service and commercial substance package (physical street address, mail scanning, resident agent, 12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed New Zealand registered office and corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a managed physical suite in Auckland or Wellington with mail handling and resident representative; not a statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence opinion and pre-incorporation governance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm engaged for pre-incorporation work
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark hourly/fixed fee for international structuring and AML compliance; no statutory maximum.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), in particular sections 10-14 (registration), 15-22 (company names), 151-158 (director requirements), 189-199 (share capital and share registers), 200-204 (financial records), and 386A (New Zealand Business Number integration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a division of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating through the Companies Register online portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company filed under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, accompanied by director consents and subscriber details; registration is perfected by the Registrar issuing a Certificate of Incorporation under section 14. Filing fee: NZ$105.20 (approximately US$64).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Companies Act 1993. The company must issue and allot at least one share; market practice is 1,000 ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each, fully or partly paid. No escrow deposit, capital contribution, or share-premium account is required before incorporation, and a wholly non-resident shareholder may own 100% of the shares without prior exchange control approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The Certificate of Incorporation issued by the New Zealand Companies Office under section 14 of the Companies Act 1993 be and is hereby received, accepted and ratified. (2) Pursuant to section 189 of the Companies Act 1993, the allotment and issue of 1,000 ordinary shares of NZ$1.00 each, fully paid, to the initial subscriber named in the application for registration be and is hereby approved, and the register of shareholders be updated accordingly. (3) The registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at the physical New Zealand street address stated in the application, and that address shall be the Company's address for service for all statutory purposes. (4) Each proposed director named in the application be and is hereby appointed as a director of the Company, and the Board appoints a Managing Director and a Company Secretary with authority to conduct the day-to-day management of the Company's business. (5) The Directors be and are hereby authorized to open and operate bank and digital payment accounts, including Apple App Store and Google Play developer payout accounts, in the Company's name. (6) Any Director or officer be authorized to execute all filings, notices and documents necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register online portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a publicly accessible search of the Companies Register to verify that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to any name already registered or reserved (Companies Act 1993, section 20). Reserve the name online for 20 working days. Avoid misleading, restricted, or objectionable terms such as 'bank', 'trust', or 'university' unless prior written approval from the relevant regulator is obtained. Prepare up to three alternative names and activate a RealMe verified identity for subsequent electronic filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and two alternative names
Brief description of the principal activity (ISIC 5820 - publishing of MMORPG software)
RealMe verified digital identity of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects to the name under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993 as being identical or confusingly similar, the applicant may submit written submissions to the Registrar for reconsideration under section 22. Alternatively, the applicant may promptly re-file with a different name. If the objection arises from a restricted word, the applicant must obtain the relevant consent or remove the offending term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Statutory Incorporation Documentation and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (pre-lodgement validation conducted through the online Companies Register system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Application for Registration of a Company in the form required by section 12 of the Companies Act 1993. Obtain executed consents to act as director from each proposed director, and record the full legal name, residential address, date and place of birth of each director. Ensure compliance with section 151: at least one director must reside in New Zealand or Australia and be a director of a New Zealand company. Record the full legal name and address of the initial shareholder, who may be a non-resident corporate entity holding 100% of the shares. Specify the allocation of shares and the registered office, which must be a physical New Zealand street address and not a post office box. Decide whether to adopt a constitution or rely on the default rules contained in the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of a Company
Executed consents to act as director (Companies Act 1993, section 152)
Shareholder and subscriber information with share allocation schedule
Consent of the registered office provider
Constitution, if any (optional; default statutory rules otherwise apply)
AML/KYC identity documentation for directors and ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory information is incomplete or any consent is unsigned or undated, the Companies Office pre-lodgement validation will flag the defect. The applicant must cure the defect and re-validate the application before formal filing. Invalid consents must be re-executed and re-dated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register using RealMe, enter the company name and statutory particulars, upload the completed application and consents, and pay the incorporation fee of NZ$105.20 electronically. The Registrar examines the application under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993 and, if satisfied, registers the company and issues the Certificate of Incorporation under section 14, which takes effect from the date and time of registration. The New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) is issued automatically upon registration.
required_dossiers: Completed incorporation application file
Director consents and shareholder consents
Electronic payment of NZ$105.20 filing fee
RealMe authenticated submission record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the application under section 13, the Registrar must provide written reasons. The applicant may correct the specified defects and re-lodge the application, or apply to the High Court for review of the Registrar's decision under section 369 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Inland Revenue Compliance Fit-Out
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - myIR secure online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated company with Inland Revenue to obtain a New Zealand IRD number and activate the myIR account. The company is tax-resident in New Zealand by virtue of incorporation and is subject to the 28% corporate income tax rate. Assess compulsory GST registration if the annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed NZ$60,000; voluntary registration may be advisable to credit input tax on development and hosting costs. If employees are engaged, register as an employer for PAYE and KiwiSaver. For a global MMORPG distributed through Apple App Store and Google Play, confirm with professional advisors which platform is responsible for New Zealand GST on remote services supplied to New Zealand consumers and confirm that the company has no New Zealand permanent establishment exposures beyond its tax-resident status.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN certificate
IRD numbers and tax file information of directors and shareholders
Company bank account details
Projected revenue and cost model from Apple App Store and Google Play payouts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD queries the registration or issued IRD number, resubmit the corrected registration through myIR with a covering explanation. Any disputed assessment may be challenged through the statutory disputes procedure, including the filing of a Notice of Proposed Adjustment and, if necessary, adjudication before the Taxation Review Authority or High Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural Board Governance, Share Registry and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's board of directors (internal governance); registered banks and non-bank deposit takers for account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and hold the inaugural board meeting. Pass the pro forma first board resolution set out in the incorporation_legal_framework. Approve the register of shareholders, issue share certificates to the initial subscriber, and record the appointments of directors and officers. Open a New Zealand dollar bank account or a reputable payment institution account in the company's name, providing complete AML/CFT due diligence documentation, and link the account to the Apple App Store and Google Play developer payout rails. File any director or officer changes with the Companies Office within 20 working days.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Minutes of the inaugural board meeting
Share certificates and share register
Bank AML/CFT onboarding forms
Proof of identity and residential address for directors and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank declines the application due to enhanced due diligence on a non-resident-owned digital publisher, the company may provide supplementary statutory declarations, audited financial statements, or evidence of the source of funds. Alternatively, the company may approach other registered banks or licensed non-bank payment service providers that accept software-publishing business models.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Due Diligence and Nil-Licence Determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of Film and Literature Classification (OFLC) for content classification; Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) for gambling licensing; Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) for environmental permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a hardcore MMORPG distributed globally through app stores, confirm that no operating, gambling, or gaming licence is required under the Gambling Act 2003 because in-app purchases do not constitute gambling unless real-money prizes or betting mechanics are offered. Self-classify the game for age rating using the OFLC classification tools if the game contains violence, sexual content, or other restricted depictions, and label the product accordingly under the Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993. Confirm that the purely digital software-publishing operation has no physical factory, plant, or discharge, and therefore no environmental or industrial site licence is required. Record the nil-licence determination in the company's compliance register.
required_dossiers: Game content self-assessment and classification output
Legal opinion memorandum confirming the absence of a gambling licence requirement
Compliance register entry recording the nil-licence determination for ISIC 5820
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the OFLC requires formal classification, the publisher must submit the game and pay the applicable fee; pending classification, New Zealand distribution must be paused if the content is likely to be objectionable. If DIA determines that any real-money element constitutes gambling, the monetization model must be restructured to remove betting or prize mechanics before launch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 5820 digital software publishing is an unlicensed activity in New Zealand, and no industrial license is issued by any authority. The general business-registration umbrella is the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) and the New Zealand Companies Office, but neither issues an operating permit for MMORPG publishing. The only ancillary regulator touching content is the Office of Film and Literature Classification, which does not grant a pre-market license but may impose classification and labeling obligations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Nil - No Operating License Required. The company's operational credentials consist solely of the Certificate of Incorporation, the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), and Inland Revenue registrations. There is no separate computer-game-publisher operating license under New Zealand law. The Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993 may require age-rated labeling of the game, but this is a content-labeling obligation and not a licensing precondition to operating the business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, in coordination with territorial authorities under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Nil / Exempt - the proposed activity is a purely digital software publishing operation with no development site, no physical plant, no discharge, and no land-use change. No resource consent, discharge permit, environmental impact assessment, or full EIA report is triggered under the Resource Management Act 1991 or the Exclusive Economic Zone and Continental Shelf (Environmental Effects) Act 2012. The activity falls wholly outside the category of activities requiring an EPA approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - the company generates no wastewater, volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, hazardous waste, or point-source discharges. If the company later leases physical office premises, the landlord's obligations under the Building Act 2004 and any territorial authority National Environmental Standards (including air quality and contaminated land) may attach to the premises, but such obligations would not arise from the publishing activity itself.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a telework or cloud-based digital operation. If a physical office is leased in New Zealand, the occupier must: (i) obtain a building warrant of fitness (BWOF) compliance schedule under the Building Act 2004 for any specified systems such as fire alarms, sprinklers, or mechanical ventilation; (ii) comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including worker engagement and participation duties and hazard management obligations; and (iii) notify WorkSafe New Zealand of any notifiable work. There is no separate 'civil defense clearance' under New Zealand law; territorial authority building inspections and fire-safety certifications satisfy all statutory requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue), New Zealand Government; sole national tax administration and tax registrar for income tax, GST, PAYE and withholding taxes. Online service portal: myIR (ird.govt.nz/myIR); official website: ird.govt.nz. Entity incorporation and NZBN registration are administered by the New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), which coordinates integrated tax registrations at formation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the NZ_LTD: registration is effected online via the Companies Office (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz); the integrated registration service automatically issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), the Companies Register number and the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number in a single filing. Step 2 - Confirm income tax registrations: the IRD number is the statutory tax file number (TIN); the company must complete its IRD file details, including director, shareholder and registered office information, through myIR; an NZ resident company is taxed on worldwide income while a non-resident company is assessed only on New Zealand-sourced income. Step 3 - Foreign-incorporated companies: an offshore company carrying on business in NZ must apply for an IRD number using form IR596 (IRD Number Application for a Non-Resident Company) supported by certified certificate of incorporation, constitution, director list, registered office address and banker confirmation; the same IRD number serves as the GST registration number. Step 4 - GST/VAT registration: statutory registration is compulsory when taxable supplies made in NZ exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period (GST Act section 51); registration is made via myIR, and non-resident suppliers of remote services may use the simplified remote-services GST registration and file quarterly returns on a pay-only (cash) basis; voluntary registration is permitted. Step 5 - Ancillary registrations: PAYE (employer withholding), fringe benefit tax, non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends, interest and royalties, and CRS/FATCA financial account declarations are completed in the same myIR account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime, but the following statutory elections materially determine classification and tax outcomes for an NZ_LTD: (1) Look-through company election (form IR525; Income Tax Act 2007 subpart HB): a close-held company with up to five look-through owners (individuals, trustees or other LTCs) may elect fiscal transparency so that income, deductions and credits flow through to shareholders; non-resident individual shareholders are permitted but taxed only on NZ-source income. (2) Imputation credit account election: a company elects (in its first income tax return) to maintain an imputation credit account so that NZ resident shareholders receive imputation credits for corporate tax paid on dividends. (3) Consolidated group and loss-grouping elections: companies within a 100% common ownership group may elect to transfer losses and file consolidated returns. (4) GST grouping election: related companies may elect to be treated as a single GST group with a nominated representative member. (5) GST accounting basis election: eligibility to account for GST on an invoice basis or payments (cash) basis; non-resident remote-services suppliers may elect the simplified pay-only basis. (6) Hybrid and branch mismatch elections: NZ applies the OECD hybrid and branch mismatch rules (subpart FH); no elective mismatch is available, but taxpayers must disclose MNE structures via IRD form IR817 and may elect ordering of the rules for dual-inclusion income and imported mismatch deductions. (7) CFC/FIF elections: the NZ parent may elect the FIF fair dividend rate method and the CFC active-business exclusion treatment for offshore gaming subsidiaries, where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - a destination-based, multi-stage value added tax imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (GST Act).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period of taxable supplies made in New Zealand. For non-resident suppliers of remote services (including downloadable MMORPG software, subscriptions and in-app purchases), the threshold tests the projected value of supplies to NZ-resident consumers over the following 12 months. Where the supply is made through an electronic marketplace such as Apple App Store or Google Play, the marketplace operator is deemed to be the supplier for GST purposes, so the NZ_LTD developer is generally not required to register for GST in respect of those NZ B2C sales; the marketplace operator collects and remits the 15% GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand mandates no real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, no continuous transaction controls and no pre-clearance API for tax invoices. A registered person must issue a GST tax invoice within 28 days for any taxable supply exceeding NZD 50 (GST-only invoices for exempt purchasers), and must retain records sufficient to verify the GST treatment. Electronic invoicing is permitted and the Government has adopted the Peppol e-invoicing framework on a voluntary basis (New Zealand Peppol Authority, MBIE); Inland Revenue itself is an early adopter. The only mandatory electronic channel is the filing of GST and income tax returns through myIR, and the electronic lodgement of customs export declarations through the Trade Single Window operated by the New Zealand Customs Service. Inland Revenue's operational practice for remote services (GST and the digital economy) requires platform suppliers to maintain digital records of the customer's location evidence, payment rail and transaction logs for audit inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% GST is available for genuine exports. Goods: the supplier must export the goods from NZ within 28 days of supply and hold contemporaneous evidence of export (section 61(1)(c) of the GST Act and the Evidence of Export Rules), namely a customs export declaration, bill of lading or air waybill. Services: supplies to a non-resident who is outside NZ when the services are performed can be zero-rated unless the services are connected with NZ land or goods in NZ. Digital gaming revenue: remote services supplied to non-resident end-customers are outside the scope of NZ GST altogether (sections 8(3) and 8C); sales to NZ consumers through Apple/Google marketplaces are deemed supplies by the marketplace operator. To substantiate the zero-rating or out-of-scope treatment, the NZ_LTD must maintain two-fold evidence of customer location and payment (device IP address, billing address, app-store payout reports, bank remittance advices) and reconcile all export lines in its GST returns and annual income tax return. If the NZ_LTD is GST-registered, it may claim input tax credits for NZ business costs and obtain cash refunds of net credits from Inland Revenue on a regular cycle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged electronically via the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing physical export and destination
Commercial Invoice and Packing List with full supplier, consignee and destination details
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign-exchange credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Executed sales contract or purchase order (for digital services: electronic supply contract, IP geo-location logs, and app-store payout statements)
GST return reconciliation worksheet identifying zero-rated export lines and the corresponding evidence of export records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue actively audits export zero-rating claims for digital exporters. Where zero-rating conditions are not met (including goods not exported within 28 days or insufficient evidence), the supply is recharacterised as taxable at 15% GST; the previously refunded output tax is clawed back with use-of-money interest from the date of refund and late payment penalties (1% per month on the unpaid amount, increasing to 2% after the first month). Tax shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 scale with culpability: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 50% for an abusive tax position and 100% for evasion, applied per affected GST period. Fraudulent zero-rating (including false customs declarations, fabricated bills of lading or counterfeit remittance certificates) is a criminal offence under section 143B, carrying fines up to NZD 250,000 for a company and director-level personal liability, together with potential asset confiscation under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009; the reassessment window extends to eight years in evasion cases and is unlimited where intent to defraud is established. Practical consequences also include deregistration of GST status, denial of refund claims, public disclosure of the assessment, and mandatory future rulings before zero-rating digital export revenue.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for market conduct; foreign exchange transfer functions rest with the Reserve Bank as the monetary authority and prudential regulator for banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a free-floating currency with full current account and capital account convertibility. No general exchange control restrictions exist under the Foreign Investment Act 2005 or exchange control regulations; non-resident profit remittances are permitted subject to standard tax withholding requirements under the Income Tax Act 2007. Dividend remittance is unrestricted, but a resident withholding tax (RWT) or non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) may apply at 15% or a reduced treaty rate. Capital repatriation is free for non-resident investors.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender obligation exists in New Zealand. Export receipts may be held in foreign currency accounts with any registered New Zealand bank, retained offshore, or converted to NZD without mandatory reporting or conversion ratios. Certain anti-money laundering record-keeping obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 apply to cross-border wire transfers of NZD 10,000 or more, but no conversion or surrender is mandated.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. New Zealand does not provide a dedicated electronic money institution (EMI) licensing category. Digital banks and non-bank financial institutions must either hold a banking licence from the Reserve Bank under the Banking Prudential Requirements or operate as a registered financial service provider and AML/CFT reporting entity under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008. Offshore EMIs may be able to partner with New Zealand-based banks for local clearing, but they cannot independently provide local domiciled accounts. Legal constraints include the need for NZX-regulated money remittance registration, a New Zealand business address, and compliance with the AML/CFT Act. For this MMORPG treasury, using an offshore EMI as a primary liquidity rail is suboptimal; direct banking with a tier-1 Australian-owned New Zealand bank is more robust.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for all directors and the ultimate beneficial owner when opening a corporate account in New Zealand for a non-resident entity, unless the bank has an established private-banking exception or accepts a prior in-person meeting at a designated New Zealand embassy or branch overseas. Remote opening is permitted in limited circumstances for low-risk corporate structures, but mandatory identity verification under AML/CFT strict liability requires biometric or chip-verified identification, a witnessed Board resolution, and a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation. In practice, at least one director must appear physically at a NZ branch or at a recognised overseas ANZ/ASB/BNZ/Westpac desk to complete signatory verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure in corporate ownership or payment flow from gaming platform providers believed to be higher-risk due to virtual assets and app-store merchant receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a comprehensive ownership map identifying every shareholder above 10%, Board resolution appointing a New Zealand-based AML compliance officer, a written business plan demonstrating the MMORPG commercial model (in-app purchase revenue), source-of-funds declarations for the initial capital injection, and a complete copy of the Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement to establish the legitimate origin of in-app purchase revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding for a non-resident corporate entity with no local physical trading address.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a registered office address in New Zealand, a physical service address of the director, notarised certified copies of passports for each director, certified Memorandum and Articles of Association, and a Certificate of Good Standing from the New Zealand Companies Office demonstrating registration and compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of intercompany loans or capital injections from offshore shareholders with complex offshore trust structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a pre-cleared capital injection letter, audited financial statements of the lending shareholder, loan agreement with arm's-length interest rates, and a Board resolution confirming the purpose of the inward remittance. Include a formal trust deed analysis if a New Zealand trust is the shareholder, to prove source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction pattern expected due to daily app-store settle lags and monthly reconciliation payouts from Apple and Google in different currencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a treasury and reconciliation policy showing forecasted daily settlement volumes, expected foreign currency exposures, and a clear financial crime risk assessment. Include an independent review of the AML/CFT programme and confirmation that no gambling or prohibited gaming activities are conducted.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: shareholder or parent company initiates a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from a corporate bank account to the NZ Ltd operational/non-resident capital account at the designated New Zealand bank. The wire instruction must include: beneficiary legal name, NZ bank BIC/SWIFT, NZ domestic account number (ANZ, ASB, BNZ or Westpac), payment purpose code 'SUPPLY' (intercompany capital contribution) or 'CAPITAL INJECTION', the NZD equivalent amount, and a tax identifier for the beneficiary. The remitter should obtain the New Zealand bank's local clearing code (e.g., ANZ 01-, ASB 12-, BNZ 02-, Westpac 03-) to ensure straight-through processing. For amounts above NZD 10,000, a completed transaction monitoring report and AML verification for the source of funds will be retained. For inward direct investment, a notification under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 is required only if the investor acquires 25% or more ownership of a significant business asset; a wholly owned NZD treasury entity used solely for capital maintenance is generally not considered significant unless the business holds sensitive land or a substantial asset value.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for intercompany supplier payments, vendor royalties, licensing fees, and cross-border operational expenses. (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) payable at sight or deferred basis for large software service licences and hosting arrangements where physical or software goods are procured from trade counterparties. (3) Local NZD clearing via the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) for domestic operational disbursements and salary payments. For recurring Apple App Store and Google Play payouts, receipts are settled via internal platform treasury runs to the entity's bank account in NZD or USD, using the platform's mandatory payout cadence and reconciliation reporting. Outbound disbursements to overseas game development studios should be executed via MT103 with purpose code 'TECH' or 'RSUPL' to ensure a clean audit trail under the AML/CFT Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla forward FX contracts up to 18 months tenor from authorized New Zealand banks (ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) for USD/NZD and AUD/NZD hedges on confirmed app-store receipts and supplier invoices.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic counterparties or where a currency lacks liquid deliverable settlement; NZD/CNH and NZD/EUR NDFs are permissible through offshore market-makers, subject to New Zealand bank counterparty limits and documentation under ISDA agreements.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for intercompany loan hedging in NZD against USD or EUR, and cross-currency basis swaps to match the currency denomination of Apple and Google settlement balances.

Lock-in forwards for future app-store payouts provided by the New Zealand bank's treasury desk, where the underlying transactional flows are identifiable and the hedge is documented under a Treasury Master Agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies - New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days after the company's annual return date, being the 12-month anniversary of incorporation; the return opens for filing one month before the due date via the NZBN or Companies Office online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZ$150 (approx. USD 90); continued default exposes the company to Registrar's 20-working-day notice of intention to remove and subsequent administrative strike-off under s.212 Companies Act 1993

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (IR4) together with financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard 31 March balance date: file by 7 July (online) or 7 June (paper); non-standard balance date: 7th day of the 7th month following balance date; tax-agent extensions apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic initial late filing penalty NZ$250 under s.141A Tax Administration Act 1994, escalating monthly incremental penalties for continued non-filing, plus use-of-money interest accruing on unpaid tax; Inland Revenue may issue default assessments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements and auditor's report (only if company is 'large' or an FMC reporting entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies - New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the balance date (extension available from the Registrar per s.201 Companies Act 1993)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under s.200/373 Companies Act 1993: fine up to NZ$50,000 on the company and on every director in default; persistent non-delivery may be treated as grounds for strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for a 'large' company meeting two of three criteria under s.45 Financial Reporting Act 2013: NZ$33 million total assets, NZ$49 million total revenue, or 60+ full-time-equivalent employees. Small companies are exempt from audit unless shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights requisition an audit under s.199 Companies Act 1993.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS (Tier 1 full or Tier 2 reduced-disclosure) for large and FMC reporting entities; simplified New Zealand XRB A1 framework (Tiers 3-4) is available for small non-FMC companies; all frameworks are IFRS-convergent

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a standalone public UBO register for ordinary private limited companies; beneficial ownership verification obligations apply only to AML/CFT reporting entities. Annually, the board must confirm in the Annual Return the complete register of members (names, addresses, and shareholdings as at the annual return date). Share transfers executed during the year must be entered in the Register of Members within 10 working days after lodgement (s.195 Companies Act 1993), and the resulting ownership structure is confirmed in the next Annual Return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 420 per annum (approx. NZ$250 - NZ$700) covering registered office address, registered agent, annual return preparation, and Companies Office compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 30,000 per annum (approx. NZ$16,000 - NZ$48,000) for a small-to-medium NZ private company subject to a full NZ IFRS independent audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not grant general tax holidays. A refundable R&D Tax Incentive (15% of eligible R&D expenditure) is available, producing an effective 13% cost offset on qualifying game-development spend. Standard business deductions apply for platform commissions (Apple/Google), streaming/hosting costs, payroll, and IP amortisation (straight-line). No patent box regime exists.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (subject to 49% shareholder continuity requirement; business continuity test applies if continuity fails)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal (or via approved tax agent software)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due by 7 July. For early balance dates (e.g., 31 December), due by 6 February of the following filing year; for late balance dates, due by 31 March of the next year. Companies represented by a registered tax agent may receive an extension to 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: gross worldwide income including Apple App Store and Google Play payouts (net of platform commissions) and any interest/dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all foreign-sourced income; NZ taxes its residents on worldwide income. If the company is controlled by non-residents, ensure transfer pricing disclosures are consistent with controlled foreign company (CFC) rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses: deductible operating expenses, including third-party platform commissions (30% on App Store, 15% on Play), server hosting, marketing, salaries, and IP amortisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be arm's length; any management fees or IP royalties paid to non-resident related parties must satisfy transfer pricing documentation and NRWT withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss (Box 1 minus Box 2) before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is a loss, verify the loss belongs to the NZ entity and is not a mispriced allocation from an offshore principal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years (subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify that no change of ownership breaches continuity; overseas shareholders' share transfers affect the continuity calculation.
Non-resident owners should ensure no exempt or foreign-sourced amounts are omitted.
Reflect only NZ statutory tax; foreign tax credits are claimed in Box 8.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: R&D tax incentive, foreign tax credits, resident withholding tax (RWT), and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach supporting schedules; foreign tax credits for Apple/Google withholding taxes (if any) must be supported by a Form IRD 128 or equivalent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: NZ$250 initial penalty plus NZ$250 per month (maximum NZ$4,000). Late payment: 1% immediately, increasing to 4% on the sixth day, plus 1% per month incremental penalty. Use-of-money interest is charged at the prescribed IRD rate (currently 8.67% per annum for 2024/25) on underpayments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (statutory rate). Resident shareholders receive fully imputed dividends (imputation credits attached at the 28% corporate tax rate).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must provide the NZ payer with a current New Zealand Inland Revenue 'Certificate of Residence' (Form IR290 or the relevant country's tax residence certificate). The payer must withhold at the reduced treaty rate only after receiving the certificate; otherwise, 30% NRWT must be withheld. Over-withheld tax can be reclaimed by the non-resident through an IR3NR return or refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties. Under widely used DTAs the rates are often 10% interest / 5% royalties (e.g., Australia, US, UK, Singapore). The Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% can apply to qualifying public-issued or listed-company interest where the payer elects to pay the levy, negating NRWT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Compulsory transfer pricing documentation for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding: NZ$1 million (services), NZ$2 million (loans/interest-bearing arrangements), and NZ$10 million (other transactions including IP royalty and goods). In addition, New Zealand groups with annual revenue exceeding NZ$50 million must maintain a TP position statement, and multinational groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750 million must file a Country-by-Country report through IRD.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute, but the 'economic substance' principle operates through the CFC regime, the branch equivalent tax rules, and general anti-avoidance provisions (Income Tax Act 2007, ss BG 1 and GA 1). A non-resident-owned NZ Ltd must have real local management, employees, and board decision-making for the MMORPG operation; otherwise, the IRD may disregard the entity or reattribute profits, and DTA benefits can be denied under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) in Article 25 of NZ's DTAs as implemented under the MLI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or under-declaring Apple/Google payout revenue; fabricating expenses; using undisclosed offshore bank accounts to receive player receipts; double-claiming R&D tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under Tax Administration Act 1994 ss 143B, 143C, 143D; fines up to NZ$250,000 for a company and up to NZ$50,000 for an individual, plus a shortfall penalty of 50% of the evaded tax, statutory interest on the unpaid amount, and imprisonment for up to five years for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted personally as primary offenders, subject to criminal fines and imprisonment. Civil liability for fraudulent trading (Companies Act 1993 s 320) allows courts to order directors to make personal restitution to creditors, and the Inland Revenue Department can seek director penalty notices for unpaid PAYE/GST and, in debt cases, for income tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a New Zealand limited company as a tax-favoured conduit for global MMORPG profits without real local presence, employees, or business decisions simply to access NZ's DTA network and 28% corporate rate; routing IP royalties through the NZ entity to a zero-tax haven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1), the IRD can cancel tax advantages and recharacterise the structure; a 100% shortfall penalty applies for a dominant purpose of tax avoidance; specific anti-treaty-shopping provisions deny treaty benefits; deemed withholding tax adjustments of 30% NRWT on recharacterised dividends can be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are knowingly involved in a sham arrangement can be held personally liable under the sham/agency principles and the Companies Act; Inland Revenue may obtain freezing orders on personal assets, and in serious cases the courts may disqualify directors and restrict international travel pending criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging below-arm's-length prices for IP licences to a related offshore distributor; inflating management fees paid to a foreign parent; failing to prepare contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Documentation above the NZD thresholds; making backdated or circular intercompany loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: An IRD transfer pricing adjustment to substitute an arm's length price, resulting in additional income tax at 28% plus use-of-money interest; a 20% shortfall penalty for failing to take reasonable care, 40% for taking an unacceptable tax position, or 100% for evasion; mandatory documentation penalties of NZ$10,000 plus NZ$2,000 per day for continued failure to provide documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be liable for shortfall penalties if they signed or approved inaccurate tax returns with wilful blindness; the Companies Act s 135 (reckless trading) allows a court to impose personal liability for creditor losses, and the IRD is a preferential creditor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: GST Evasion on Remote Digital Services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register for New Zealand GST on 'remote services' (digital game subscriptions and in-app virtual items supplied to New Zealand consumers); charging GST at 15% but not remitting it; claiming inappropriate input credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compulsory GST registration is required from the first NZ$60,000 of supplies to NZ consumers; evasion triggers a notional GST assessment at 15%, a 100% shortfall penalty for evasion, and late payment penalties; a fine of up to NZ$250,000 and forfeiture of assets under the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the NZ company can be made personally liable for GST debts under the director penalty regime (ss 161H-161J Tax Administration Act 1994) if the company fails to pay GST in dissolution or liquidation; travel bans can be imposed under the District Court Act for non-compliance with assessment orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating informal digital payment processing or virtual currency wallets for MMORPG players without registration as an AML/CFT reporting entity; failing to file suspicious transaction reports (STRs) for large in-app purchase flows; ignoring sanctions screening on global players.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, civil penalties for each breach can be up to NZ$800,000 for a company and NZ$160,000 for individuals; criminal penalties for reckless money laundering carry imprisonment up to 7 years; the AML/CFT supervisor can issue compliance notices and suspend the entity's operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed for knowing participation in money laundering (Crimes Act 1961 s 243); the High Court can impose director disqualification orders and asset freezing; non-resident directors are not immune and may face extradition or travel bans for AML offences committed in New Zealand.
